onboarding_ready.message: Got it. All done, thank you! One idea for you: You said you walk. Make a playlist of upbeat songs and match your steps to the beat for a song or two, then cool off with a slower one. More ideas are on the next screen.

mascot_events.caption: Got it. All done, thank you! One idea for you: You said you walk. Make a playlist of upbeat songs and match your steps to the beat for a song or two, then cool off with a slower one. More ideas are on the next screen.

recommendations.title: Walk to the beat
recommendations.message: You said you walk. Make a playlist of upbeat songs and match your steps to the beat for a song or two, then cool off with a slower one.
recommendations.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
recommendations.why_short: A quick beat makes a faster pace feel easy.

alternatives.title: Brisk walks with friends
alternatives.message: You said you walk. Walk with a friend at a pace where you can talk but not sing. You'll keep each other going a bit faster than you'd go alone.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: A walking partner helps you keep a brisker pace.

alternatives.title: Find a hill
alternatives.message: You said you walk. Add a hill or a slope to your usual route and climb it at a steady push. Walking uphill turns an easy walk into a livelier one.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: A hill adds effort to your usual walk.

alternatives.title: Lamppost intervals
alternatives.message: You said you walk. On your next walk, pick up the pace between two lampposts, then ease off for the next two, and keep swapping. Brisk bits that leave you a little out of breath count double.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Faster stretches are a simple next step for walkers.

recommendations.title: Move in the daytime
recommendations.message: You said you go to bed around 11. Being active during the day, like a walk in the afternoon, can make it easier to fall asleep at night. Just finish brisk exercise a few hours before bed.
recommendations.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
recommendations.why_short: Daytime activity can make it easier to fall asleep.

alternatives.title: A bedtime alarm
alternatives.message: You said you go to bed around 11. Set an alarm for bedtime, not just for waking. When it goes off, start winding down, even if it's in the middle of a show.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: A reminder at bedtime helps you keep a regular schedule.

alternatives.title: Morning daylight
alternatives.message: You said you go to bed around 11. Get outside into daylight soon after you wake, even for a few minutes with your coffee on the porch or on a short stroll. Morning light helps set your body clock.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Morning light helps set your body clock.

alternatives.title: Screens off early
alternatives.message: You said you go to bed around 11. Put phones, laptops and the TV away about half an hour before bed, and charge your phone outside the bedroom if you can.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Screens off before bed make it easier to drift off.

recommendations.title: Shift and reach
recommendations.message: Every hour, change position, sit up tall, and reach both arms overhead and out to the sides a few times. Small moves break up long spells of stillness.
recommendations.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
recommendations.why_short: Small moves in your seat break up stillness.

alternatives.title: A show-time stretch
alternatives.message: During each show, do a few seated stretches: stretch and flex your feet, circle your ankles and roll your shoulders.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Moving in your seat breaks up long sitting.

alternatives.title: Stand for the ads
alternatives.message: Each time the ads come on, stand up and move around the room until your show is back. Over an evening, it adds up.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Standing for each ad break breaks up long sitting.

alternatives.title: Remote across the room
alternatives.message: Keep the TV remote across the room, so changing the channel means a few steps each time.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: A few extra steps each time break up long sitting.

Pick something you'd love to spend it on, like a meal out with friends or a gift for someone special. When you're ready, 1-800-QUIT-NOW offers free support. You'll keep your routine going, and you might get them moving too.

alternatives.title: Support for quitting
alternatives.message: Quitting smoking helps health at any age. When you feel ready, you could call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free, friendly support.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Support is there whenever you feel ready to quit.

alternatives.title: Breathe through a craving
alternatives.message: When a craving comes, try slow breathing: in through your nose while you count to four, out through your mouth while you count to six. A few rounds can take the edge off the urge. When you're ready, 1-800-QUIT-NOW offers free support.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Slow breathing gives a craving time to pass.

alternatives.title: Tell someone you trust
alternatives.message: Tell a friend or someone in your family that you're thinking about quitting, and ask if you can text them when a craving gets hard. Having someone in your corner can make the tough moments easier. When you're ready, 1-800-QUIT-NOW offers free support.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Quitting is easier with someone cheering you on.

lines: Here's a small plan for today.
Hold a kitchen counter. Stand with one foot right in front of the other, heel to toe, then switch feet, for 5 minutes.
Try adding some protein to each meal, like eggs, beans, yogurt or fish. If your doctor has told you to limit protein, follow that.
When an ad comes on, stand up and move around until the show is back.
You moved on 6 days this week. Nice rhythm!

items.title: Heel-to-toe stand, holding the counter
items.message: Hold a kitchen counter. Stand with one foot right in front of the other, heel to toe, then switch feet, for 5 minutes.
items.why: Strength and balance moves help keep you steady on your feet.
based_on: checkins.6 logged days this week, minutes
items.source_title: USPSTF 2024: exercise to prevent falls in older adults (AAFP summary)

items.title: Some protein at each meal
items.message: Try adding some protein to each meal, like eggs, beans, yogurt or fish. If your doctor has told you to limit protein, follow that.
items.why: Many older adults don't get enough protein, and it helps keep muscles strong.
items.source_title: ACL: Nutrition needs of older adults, protein

items.title: Up during the ad breaks
items.message: When an ad comes on, stand up and move around until the show is back.
items.why: Breaking up long sitting is good for everyone, whatever else you do.
items.source_title: WHO 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour

lines: Here's today's plan.
You said heel-to-toe stand, holding the counter hurt your knee, so today is gentle on the knees: walking in the pool.
Walk back and forth in the shallow end of a pool for 15 minutes. The water is gentle on sore joints.
Try adding some protein to each meal, like eggs, beans, yogurt or fish. If your doctor has told you to limit protein, follow that.
When an ad comes on, stand up and move around until the show is back.
I'm sorry you're not feeling your best. Rest is fine, and gentle is good.

recommendations_after_weekly.message: Here are a few ideas from what you told me. Every hour, change position, sit up tall, and reach both arms overhead and out to the sides a few times. Small moves break up long spells of stillness. You're already active, walking, at about 210 minutes a week. That's at or above the 150 minutes adults are advised to aim for. Keep it up! Alongside what you do, the guidelines also suggest muscle-strengthening moves on two days a week, like carrying groceries, heavy gardening or resistance bands.

recommendations.title: Shift and reach
recommendations.message: Every hour, change position, sit up tall, and reach both arms overhead and out to the sides a few times. Small moves break up long spells of stillness.
recommendations.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
recommendations.why_short: Small moves in your seat break up stillness.

alternatives.title: A show-time stretch
alternatives.message: During each show, do a few seated stretches: stretch and flex your feet, circle your ankles and roll your shoulders.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Moving in your seat breaks up long sitting.

alternatives.title: Stand for the ads
alternatives.message: Each time the ads come on, stand up and move around the room until your show is back. Over an evening, it adds up.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Standing for each ad break breaks up long sitting.

alternatives.title: Remote across the room
alternatives.message: Keep the TV remote across the room, so changing the channel means a few steps each time.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: A few extra steps each time break up long sitting.

recommendations.title: Strong and active
recommendations.message: You're already active, walking, at about 210 minutes a week. That's at or above the 150 minutes adults are advised to aim for. Keep it up! Alongside what you do, the guidelines also suggest muscle-strengthening moves on two days a week, like carrying groceries, heavy gardening or resistance bands.
recommendations.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
recommendations.why_short: Strength moves round out the activity you already do.

alternatives.title: Add a little balance
alternatives.message: You're already active, walking, at about 210 minutes a week. That's at or above the 150 minutes adults are advised to aim for. Keep it up! The guidelines for older adults also suggest balance activities, like standing on one foot while you hold the kitchen counter, or walking heel to toe along the hall.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Balance practice rounds out the activity you already do.

alternatives.title: Bring someone along
alternatives.message: You're already active, walking, at about 210 minutes a week. That's at or above the 150 minutes adults are advised to aim for. Keep it up! Invite a friend or neighbor to join you now and then. You'll keep your routine going, and you might get them moving too.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: Sharing what you do helps you keep it going.

alternatives.title: Mix it up
alternatives.message: You're already active, walking, at about 210 minutes a week. That's at or above the 150 minutes adults are advised to aim for. Keep it up! To keep it fun, swap in something new now and then, like a new walking route, a swim or a dance class.
alternatives.effect_note: Modeled difference for people like you, not a promise.
alternatives.why_short: You're already active, so keep doing what works.
